answer.evidence: Both the top cap of the lantern (rows 2-9) and the rounded base plinth (rows 38-43) are rendered with distinct foreshortened elliptical top surfaces appropriate for 3/4 top-down perspective.

answer.main_body: gas street lamp (lantern head, iron pole, and base)
answer.evidence: The top lantern cap is drawn foreshortened from above (rows 2-10, approx. 9 rows tall) with the front rim curving downward in a downward-facing arc (row 12 at center, row 9-10 at sides). The pedestal base also shows its top domed surface across rows 38-43 (6 rows).

The lantern cap shows its top surface spanning rows 2-10 in 3/4 view, with the finial placed on the upper slope (rows 4-6) allowing the back curve of the dome to show behind it (rows 2-3). The base also shows a 5-row top dome surface (rows 38-42).

The cylindrical base plinth shows a clear top surface spanning rows 38 to 43 (approx. 6 rows) viewed from above before dropping into the vertical front face on rows 44-47. The lantern cap and collar rings also reflect the 3/4 downward camera angle.
